title: Sunday half Ironman: open-water swim unfuelled, bike and run at 60-90 g an hour
message: Can you plan my meals for next week, {Mon} to {Sun}? I'm racing a half Ironman (70.3) on Sunday and I'm aiming for about 5h15. The swim is in a lake.
Tuesday: 45 min pool swim with 8 x 100 m hard, then 40 min easy run
Wednesday: 1h30 ride with 2 x 15 min at race pace
Thursday: 40 min run with 3 x 5 min at threshold
Saturday: 30 min easy bike with a few short efforts and a 10 min jog
I weigh 66 kg and live in Australia. No restrictions. I've got half a bag of spinach and some Greek yoghurt to use up.
That's everything — please go ahead and make the plan.

judge.question: Taken as food for the whole race, does the race's `during` example add up to roughly its hourly carbohydrate range over the time the athlete expects to take? Count about 30–40 g for a 500 ml bottle of isotonic drink, 21–27 g for an energy gel, 43 g for an energy bar and 27 g for a banana.

The race's swim is in open water, and the skill's rule is that an open-water swim has no carbohydrate during it. Does nothing in the plan or the reply tell the athlete to take carbohydrate during the swim? A plan that says nothing about the swim answers yes.
